title: Rollout Handoff & Metrics Checklist (collab working doc)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures the cross-functional handoff checklist, metric definitions, and phased traffic plan for canary / A-B style rollouts of Console-driven experiments. It is intentionally pragmatic: quick checks to reduce blast radius and a common vocabulary for Product, Eng, SRE, Applied ML, and Solutions.

Status / context notes:
- Drafted during runway planning for the Q4 rollout of adaptive batching and cache-aware routing.
- Not an org-level policy — intended as a repeatable working template for product + infra rollouts.
- TODO: convert to a formal playbook once we validate 3 runs end-to-end.

Audience:
- Product managers (feature owners)
- Release/Platform engineers (who configure traffic slices)
- SRE/on-call (monitoring and rollback)
- Applied ML (model variant compatibility, quality monitoring)
- PMM/CS for customer comms where customers are impacted

Quick ownership summary (who must sign off before traffic ramp):
- Feature lead (Product) — feature readiness, acceptance metrics defined
- Release eng / Platform — routing config, feature flags, traffic slicing tested
- SRE — alert thresholds, dashboards, rollback plan approved
- Applied ML — quality checks, eval sets, baseline & guardrails
- Security/Privacy (if data path changes) — sign-off for handling customer data

Acceptance & gating metrics (examples; feature owner to define exact queries):
Primary product acceptance metrics (examples):
- Conversion / success-rate (primary business KPI) — metric name: feature.primary_success_rate. Baseline: 14-day avg. Gate: delta <= 1.5% absolute or relative threshold defined in PRD.
- Latency p95 for user visible calls — metric: api.latency.p95.featureRoute. Gate: must be <= baseline + 30% or absolute 300ms cap (whichever is stricter).
- Error rate (5xx) at route level — metric: api.errors. Gate: no sustained >2x baseline for >5m.

Model/Quality metrics (for ML-powered features):
- Regression rate on golden promptset — metric: eval.regressions.count. Gate: zero regressions on blocking prompts OR manual triage accepts reasoned quality tradeoff.
- Embedding similarity distribution shift — metric: embeddings.cosine.shift. Gate: no >10% drop in downstream retrieval recall.

Operational metrics (SRE priorities):
- GPU queue length and scheduling latency — metric: infra.gpu.queue.mean. Gate: under threshold to avoid queue times > Xs.
- Token cost per response — metric: billing.tokens.per_response. Gate: cost delta within product tolerance.
- Autoscaler activity / OOMs — Gate: no OOMs or unexpected scale flapping.

Experiment design template (fill this before any rollout):
- Experiment name / id: 
- Owner / PM: 
- Hypothesis (one line): 
- Primary metric + measurement window: 
- Secondary metrics: (list)
- Control description: (model version, routing path)
- Treatment description: (model variant, quantization, batching config)
- Traffic slicing method: (cookie-based, header, region, percent)
- Randomization seed and allocation mechanism: 
- Data capture: which logs/trace fields to store (include sample payload redaction rule)
- Success criteria & stop criteria: (clear, measurable)

Traffic ramp & phasing (example sequence to use as a template):
- Phase 0: Dry-run / shadow (0% traffic) for 24-48h to validate logs & metrics. Verify correlations and debug traces.
- Phase 1: 1% global traffic for 30 minutes. Check infra and primary metrics.
- Phase 2: 5% for 1 hour. Expand checks, confirm no customer-facing regressions.
- Phase 3: 20% for 2 hours. Focus on load, queueing, cost.
- Phase 4: 50% for 4 hours (if safe). Run extended A/B analysis.
- Phase 5: 100% rollout OR rollback. Post-rollout monitoring window: 72 hours recommended for infra-heavy changes.
Notes:
- Ramp durations should be longer for customer-facing regressions or high-cost changes.
- For region-specific rollouts, start with non-critical region (eu-west/asia-south depending on privacy).
- Always run a smoke rollback drill in staging before Phase 1.

Observability & instrumentation checklist (must be validated before Phase 1):
- Metrics (time series): primary, secondary, infra. Confirm these are exported to metrics backend and have alerts on cardinality/ingestion.
- Tracing: end-to-end traces for a sample of requests including A/B tag and model variant id. Span for tokenization, model infer, post-process.
- Logs: structured logs with request id, experiment id, variant id, route, error codes. Redaction rules applied for user text.
- Dashboards: create a temporary run dashboard with comparison panels (Control vs Treatment). Templates: product_compare.tpl, infra_health.tpl.
- Cost signals: token-level cost and GPU hours by experiment tag.
- Canary probes: synthetic traffic scripts running key flows (auth, generate, embed) with SLAs.

Alerting & Runbook snippets (SRE):
- Alert bucket: TrafficRegressionCritical — triggers on primary metric falling below gate for 10m. Owner: oncall-sre.
- Alert bucket: InfraBackpressure — GPU queue > threshold for 5m. Owner: infra-oncall.
- Runbook step 1: Identify impacted cohort (experiment id + variant). Pull compare dashboard.
- Runbook step 2: If infra issue -> route all traffic to control or autoscale pool; if feature quality -> disable routing for treatment via flag.
- Runbook step 3: Notify PM + ML owner in slack channel #rollouts (include run id).
- Runbook step 4: Rollback criteria checklist (see below).

Rollback criteria (examples to be concretized per experiment):
- Any sustained >2x error rate for 10 minutes affecting >1% of requests.
- Primary business KPI drop >3% absolute for >30 minutes.
- Critical infra degradation (GPU OOMs, autoscaler unable to keep up) lasting >5 minutes.
- Any privacy/security incident.
Rollback mechanism options (choose & test ahead of time):
- Feature flag flip (fastest) — must be tested in prod staging previously.
- Traffic re-route at gateway to control variant — requires runbook and platform eng involvement.
- Reduce treatment weight gradually if partial issues appear.

Communication cadence & templates (internal + customer):
- Pre-launch: 48h heads-up email to SRE, infra, applied-ml, customer-success, legal (if required). Include run id and slack channel.
- Launch day: Start channel in slack #rollouts-run-<id>. Post phase milestones (0,1,2,3) with short status (OK / Investigating / Rollback).
- Post-rollback: 1-hour postmortem summary to stakeholders; 24-hour detailed incident report if rollback triggered.
- Customer comms: PS + CS draft templated blurb if customers observe regressions (PM to coordinate).

Ownership matrix (who must do what before Phase 1) — checklist style:
- Product (owner): finalize acceptance metrics, confirm experiment hypothesis, populate experiment template.
- Applied ML: prepare regression prompt set, run eval baseline, confirm no blocking regression.
- Platform eng: routing config ready in infra repo + dry-run tested.
- SRE: dashboards created, alerts & runbook drafted, oncall rotated for launch window.
- Security/Legal: confirm data handling for logs and synthetic probes.
- CS/PMM: comms templates and impact classification ready.

Data retention & privacy notes:
- Keep experiment request/response payloads only for as long as necessary and in accordance with the redaction policy.
- Use sampling for full-text storage (1:1000 unless explicit user opt-in).
- If treatment touches user PII or customer-configured files, get security signoff and increase retention scrutiny.

Post-launch analysis (what to run after full rollout or rollback):
- A/B statistical test run (include pre-analysis plan — avoid p-hacking).
- Regression triage log with links to failing prompts and triage owner.
- Cost analysis: token-hours and incremental GPU cost vs baseline.
- Performance heatmap: p50/p95/p99 comparisons by region and client.
- Lessons learned checklist for playbook updates.

Open questions / unresolved items (notes to self):
- How do we standardize delta thresholds across different customer segments? Right now thresholds are feature-defined.
- Do we want a single "rollout coordinator" role for each launch? Might reduce handoff confusion.
- Need a standardized synthetic probe repo for canary flows (assigned to infra team).
- Should we integrate experiment ids into billing tags? Would help cost attribution.

Practical examples & short case study (internal):
- Reference run: RL-2025-09-batching — we used a 0/1/5/25/100 ramp over 72h; the gating thresholds caught a small p95 latency spike at 5% which was traced to a cache-miss bug. We rolled back to 1% for 3h, patched, then resumed. Outcome: no customer-facing incidents, cost delta +3% but better throughput.

Checklist before Phase 1 (quick tick box for launch owner):
- [ ] Experiment template completed and reviewed
- [ ] Dashboards & alerts in place
- [ ] Instrumentation verified with sample traces
- [ ] SRE oncall assigned and runbook shared
- [ ] Routing config tested in staging
- [ ] Security sign-off (if required)
- [ ] Communication plan shared with CS/PMM

Appendix: Helpful links & templates
- Experiment template (confluence): confluence/ROLLOUT-templates-2025
- Run dashboard templates: grafana/templates/rollout-run.tpl
- Example SQL for primary metric (copy & adapt):
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('minute', event_ts) as minute,
    SUM(case when outcome = 'success' then 1 else 0 end)::float / COUNT(*) as success_rate
  FROM events.feature_exec
  WHERE experiment_id = '{{experiment_id}}' AND event_ts >= '{{start}}' AND event_ts < '{{end}}'
  GROUP BY 1
  ORDER BY 1;

Notes: keep this doc light and pragmatic. We expect each product area to adapt thresholds and add feature-specific probes. Once we've validated across 3 different run types (ML quality, infra change, pricing tweak) we'll elevate this into a canonical playbook and automate parts of the checklist in the Console UI.

If you're reviewing: add comments inline in this doc or ping me (Priya) — I'll consolidate before next week.
